fault-01.x3d.viewer_sees: Only the glowing lamp bulb; the table and floor stay black.
fault-01.x3d.nearest_prior: P077: there the scene has no light at all; here a light exists but its scope excludes the objects it is meant to light.
fault-01.x3d.fault: The DirectionalLight sits inside the lamp fixture's Transform with the default global='false', so it lights only the fixture's own children and not the table or floor.
fault-01.x3d.prose: A ceiling lamp fixture lights the table and the floor of a small room; the viewer's headlight is off.

fault-02.x3d.viewer_sees: The pillars are black against the dark sky; only the part of the pole near the lantern is lit.
fault-02.x3d.nearest_prior: P077: closest listed lighting fault (no light at all); here the light is on but its radius ends before the lit objects.
fault-02.x3d.fault: The PointLight radius is 3, less than the distance to any pillar, so the light reaches none of them.
fault-02.x3d.prose: A lantern on a pole lights the three pillars standing five metres around it; the viewer's headlight is off.

fault-03.x3d.viewer_sees: A white ball instead of a copper one.
fault-03.x3d.spec: error per the X3D standard (PhysicalMaterial has no diffuseColor field; Shape component, PhysicalMaterial interface)
fault-03.x3d.nearest_prior: P031: a PhysicalMaterial value out of range; here a field from the classic Material is used on the physical one.
fault-03.x3d.fault: PhysicalMaterial is given a diffuseColor attribute; it has no such field (its colour field is baseColor), so the colour is dropped.
fault-03.x3d.prose: A copper-coloured ball with a physically based surface.

fault-04.x3d.viewer_sees: The axes are visible but the curve is black on black, so it cannot be seen.
fault-04.x3d.nearest_prior: none: no listed mistake concerns the colour of line geometry.
fault-04.x3d.fault: The curve's colour is put in diffuseColor; lines are not lit and take their colour from emissiveColor, which is left black.
fault-04.x3d.prose: A yellow line chart with two grey axes drawn against the default black background.

fault-05.x3d.viewer_sees: No checker pattern (the texture is rejected or the last pixel is undefined).
fault-05.x3d.spec: error per the X3D standard (SFImage: width*height pixel values shall follow the three header numbers)
fault-05.x3d.nearest_prior: P067: a count mismatch in TextureCoordinate; here the mismatch is in the pixel data of the image itself.
fault-05.x3d.fault: The PixelTexture image declares 2 x 2 pixels but lists only three pixel values.
fault-05.x3d.prose: A square tile carries a two by two red and white checker pattern.

fault-06.x3d.viewer_sees: One small copy of the brick picture in a corner with its edge pixels smeared across the rest of the wall.
fault-06.x3d.nearest_prior: P112: there the TextureTransform scale was inverted; here the scale is right but repetition is switched off on the texture.
fault-06.x3d.fault: repeatS and repeatT are false, so texture coordinates beyond 0..1 are clamped and the picture cannot tile.
fault-06.x3d.prose: A wall is covered with a brick picture repeated four times across and four times up.

fault-07.x3d.nearest_prior: P067: too few texture coordinates; here the count is right but the vertical axis is inverted.
fault-07.x3d.fault: The texture coordinates assume the image origin is at the top left; X3D puts t=0 at the bottom, so the picture is mapped upside down.
fault-07.x3d.prose: A signboard shows the arrow picture upright, with the arrow pointing up.

fault-08.x3d.viewer_sees: The corners show the wrong colours (red, yellow-ish, magenta, and so on) or the colours are rejected.
fault-08.x3d.spec: error per the X3D standard (MFColor values are triples; 16 numbers is not a whole number of colours)
fault-08.x3d.nearest_prior: P106: colours applied per vertex instead of per face; here the colour tuples themselves have the wrong arity for the node.
fault-08.x3d.fault: Four-component RGBA values are written into a Color node, which holds three-component colours, so the 16 numbers are regrouped as five and a third wrong colours.
fault-08.x3d.prose: A square panel whose four corners are red, green, blue and yellow, blending smoothly across the face.

fault-09.x3d.viewer_sees: No pane at all: the ball is seen untinted against the bright background.
fault-09.x3d.nearest_prior: P111: transparency 1 used for opaque; here the transparency value is right but the alpha mode discards the surface.
fault-09.x3d.fault: The pane's Appearance uses alphaMode MASK; with the default alphaCutoff 0.5 its alpha of 0.3 is below the cutoff, so the whole pane is discarded.
fault-09.x3d.prose: A blue-tinted glass pane stands in front of a yellow ball, and the ball is seen through the tint.

fault-10.x3d.viewer_sees: No sign text, or the words split into separate lines.
fault-10.x3d.spec: error per the X3D standard (XML encoding: MFString values are quoted strings)
fault-10.x3d.nearest_prior: none: no listed mistake concerns string quoting.
fault-10.x3d.fault: The Text string is written as bare words; it is an MFString and each string must be enclosed in double quotes.
fault-10.x3d.prose: A station sign shows the words Platform 9 on one line.

fault-11.x3d.viewer_sees: The title starts at the doorway's centre line and runs off to the right instead of being centred.
fault-11.x3d.spec: error per the X3D standard (FontStyle justify enumeration)
fault-11.x3d.nearest_prior: none: no listed mistake concerns FontStyle.
fault-11.x3d.fault: FontStyle justify is "CENTER", which is not one of the allowed values (BEGIN, FIRST, MIDDLE, END).
fault-11.x3d.prose: The title GALLERY is centred left to right above the middle of the doorway.

fault-12.x3d.viewer_sees: All posts are equally vivid red; there is no mist.
fault-12.x3d.nearest_prior: P094: a sensor left at a disabling default size; here the node and field are different (Fog range) though the pattern of a disabling default is similar.
fault-12.x3d.fault: The Fog has a colour and type but no visibilityRange; the default 0 means no fog at all.
fault-12.x3d.prose: A row of red posts recedes into pale mist, each post fainter than the one before, the farthest almost gone.

fault-13.x3d.viewer_sees: Deep blue at the horizon and orange straight overhead.
fault-13.x3d.nearest_prior: P039: the number of sky colours did not match the angles; here the count is right and the order is reversed.
fault-13.x3d.fault: The sky colours are listed from the horizon upward; skyColor starts at the zenith, so the gradient is upside down.
fault-13.x3d.prose: An evening sky: deep blue overhead fading to orange at the horizon, above dark ground.

fault-14.x3d.viewer_sees: The floor is evenly lit with no shadow under the ball.
fault-14.x3d.nearest_prior: none: no listed mistake concerns shadows.
fault-14.x3d.fault: The light sets shadowIntensity but leaves shadows at its default false, so no shadow is cast.
fault-14.x3d.prose: A ball hovers over a floor and the sun throws its shadow on the floor; the viewer's headlight is off.

fault-15.x3d.viewer_sees: On the first drag the vase swings out of view instead of turning in place.
fault-15.x3d.nearest_prior: P114: a viewpoint looking the wrong way; here the view is right at load and the orbit centre is wrong.
fault-15.x3d.fault: The Viewpoint keeps the default centerOfRotation 0 0 0 although the vase is at 30 1 0, so examining orbits around empty space thirty metres away.
fault-15.x3d.prose: A vase stands thirty metres east of the origin and the viewer examines it by orbiting around it.

fault-16.x3d.viewer_sees: A distorted or empty view instead of the 8 by 6 plan with four corner blocks.
fault-16.x3d.nearest_prior: P076: a perspective fieldOfView given in degrees; here it is the four-number orthographic window with its components in the wrong order.
fault-16.x3d.fault: The OrthoViewpoint fieldOfView is written as left right bottom top; the field order is minX minY maxX maxY, so the box is read as x from -4 to -3 and y from 4 to 3.
fault-16.x3d.prose: A floor plan seen straight from above in a parallel view eight metres wide and six metres deep, showing all four corner blocks.

fault-17.x3d.viewer_sees: The railing and empty sky; the towers are clipped away.
fault-17.x3d.nearest_prior: P037: an object placed absurdly far away; here the object is at a sensible distance and the navigation setting cuts it off.
fault-17.x3d.fault: visibilityLimit is 25, so the far clipping plane lies in front of the towers at 60 metres.
fault-17.x3d.prose: From the terrace the viewer sees the near railing and, across the water, the two distant towers on the far shore.

fault-18.x3d.viewer_sees: A box when close and the smooth sphere only when far away.
fault-18.x3d.nearest_prior: P060: the LOD range values were out of order; here the range is right and the children are in the wrong order.
fault-18.x3d.fault: The LOD children are listed coarsest first; the first child is the one shown nearest, so the versions are used in reverse.
fault-18.x3d.prose: A globe is drawn as a smooth sphere when the viewer is close, as a simpler drum at middle distance and as a plain box from far away; the view starts close.

fault-19.x3d.viewer_sees: The tower stays a plain box even when the camera is right in front of it.
fault-19.x3d.nearest_prior: P120: a Transform turning about the wrong point because center was omitted; here it is the LOD's distance reference point, a different node and effect.
fault-19.x3d.fault: The LOD keeps its default center 0 0 0 although every level is drawn a hundred metres away, so the distance is measured to the origin and never falls inside the first range.
fault-19.x3d.prose: The camera flies in towards a tower that stands a hundred metres east of the origin, and on arrival the tower is shown in its finest version.

fault-20.x3d.viewer_sees: Silence at the radio; the hum is only heard near the empty origin.
fault-20.x3d.nearest_prior: P092: a sensor placed in the wrong part of the tree; here it is a sound source positioned away from the object it belongs to.
fault-20.x3d.fault: The Sound is a sibling of the radio's Transform and has no location, so it is emitted at the origin with a ten-metre reach, forty metres from the radio and the visitor.
fault-20.x3d.prose: A radio on a table at the far end of a long hall hums, and a visitor standing in front of the radio hears it.

decoy-01.x3d.intent: each case is lit only by its own scoped light
decoy-01.x3d.why_suspicious: The headlight is off and both lights are non-global (the default), which often leaves a scene dark; here each light sits in the same group as the shape it is meant to light, so the scoping is exactly what is wanted.
decoy-01.x3d.prose: Two display cases, each lit only by its own lamp, one warm and one cool; the viewer's headlight is off.

decoy-02.x3d.intent: three text lines (the middle one blank) centred both ways
decoy-02.x3d.why_suspicious: An empty string inside the MFString, a Billboard with axisOfRotation 0 0 0 and a diffuse-black emissive material all look like slips; the empty string is a legal blank line, the zero axis means viewer-aligned, and the emissive colour keeps the text bright.
decoy-02.x3d.prose: A two-line signpost with a blank line between NORTH and SOUTH, centred on its post and always facing the viewer.

decoy-03.x3d.intent: a narrow field of view from far away frames the cube
decoy-03.x3d.why_suspicious: visibilityLimit 0 looks like a zero clip distance but means no limit; fieldOfView 0.05 looks like a typo but is a legal narrow angle that frames the cube from 80 m; one sky angle with two colours is the correct n+1 pairing.
decoy-03.x3d.prose: A telephoto view of a small red cube from eighty metres, under a sky with a single band and no far clipping limit.

decoy-04.x3d.intent: the last level is deliberately empty so the beacon vanishes beyond 50 m
decoy-04.x3d.why_suspicious: An empty Group as the last LOD child and two range values for three children look like an unfinished node; an empty last level is the standard way to cull by distance and n-1 ranges for n children is correct.
decoy-04.x3d.prose: A beacon is shown in detail up close, simplified further off, and not drawn at all once the camera has backed far away.

decoy-05.x3d.intent: an unlit one-component texture tiled by a texture transform, and per-polyline colours
decoy-05.x3d.why_suspicious: A textured Shape with no Material, a PixelTexture with one-byte pixels, a line set with no Appearance at all and two colours for five vertices all look incomplete; each is legal: the texture is shown unlit, intensity pixels are one byte, and with colorPerVertex false there is one colour per polyline.
decoy-05.x3d.prose: A grey checkerboard tile repeated four times each way with crisp pixel edges, next to a zigzag made of one red and one green stroke.
